entries.title: II Timothy 2:4
segments: Who enrolled him. The soldier's allegiance is to his commander and his cause.  Paul urges an undivided allegiance upon Timothy.

entries.title: II Timothy 2:5
segments: Lawfully. According to the rules of the game.  Hardships are a part of the soldier's service.

entries.title: II Timothy 2:8
segments: Of the seed of David. That is, Christ, a man in the flesh, and risen from the dead in the flesh.

entries.title: II Timothy 2:9
segments:
As a malefactor. Subject to the indignity of being chained to a soldier.
 

 
 The word of God is not bound. Even in his imprisonment Paul preached the truth to the soldiers of the guard (
), and by his letters reached a larger congregation than he could have done with his preaching.

entries.title: II Timothy 2:11
segments: Died with him. As to the desires of the flesh.  See

entries.title: II Timothy 2:12
segments: Reign with him. See

entries.title: II Timothy 2:13
segments: He abideth faithful. He cannot deny his own nature; he must deny everything unlike himself.  If we do not accept him we place ourselves under condemnation.

entries.title: II Timothy 2:14
segments: About words. The warning here is against giving such attention to the words in which the gospel is presented that its vital truth is entirely lost.  The letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life (
).  See

entries.title: II Timothy 2:19
segments: The firm foundation. The unchanging truth of God, 'with whom can be no variation, neither shadow that is cast by turning' (
).  In this connection Paul was probably speaking of the resurrection of Jesus as the foundation upon which Christianity was built.  See

entries.title: II Timothy 2:20
segments: A great house. The parallel is drawn with the church.  Not all receive the gifts of grace in equal measure.  See

entries.title: II Timothy 2:21
segments: From these. Probably the false teachings spoken of in
. See

entries.title: II Timothy 2:23
segments: Ignorant questionings. Questions which arise in a mind lacking in understanding.

entries.title: II Timothy 2:25
segments: Give them repentance. The consequences to those who oppose teaching, and who wilfully 'refuse to have God in their knowledge,' are described in
.  Repentance to such as these comes as the mercy of God.  See

entries.title: II Timothy 2:26
segments: The snare of the devil. in this connection the snare operated through the distorting of doctrine in men's minds, leading them through a maze of reasonings having the form of godliness but not the reality (
).  See
